items.headline: BMW Group delivered 2.46 million cars in 2025, up 0.5%
items.driver: Growth in Europe and the US offset subdued demand in China; electrified models in high demand.
items.customer_relevance: Premium buyers in Europe/US still growing; global volume flat, so growth depends on regional fit.
items.quote: The BMW Group delivered a total of 2,463,715 vehicles to customers in 2025 – an increase of +0.5% year-on-year.
items.notes: Provisional; BMW Group Report 2025 (Mar 2026) final figure is 2,463,681.

items.headline: China mandates AEB as standard on light vehicles from 2028

items.driver: SAMR/SAC approved first mandatory safety baseline for combined driver assistance incl. NOA after rapid adoption.

items.notes: Gloss: 'Intelligent connected vehicles - safety requirements for combined driver assistance systems'. '拟于2027年1月1日起正式实施' (effective 1 Jan 2027). MIIT approval date reported as 27 Jun 2026.

items.headline: L2 standard: hands/eyes monitoring, 72h NOA road tests, 2028 for existing models

items.notes: Gloss: when active, the system must continuously monitor the driver's hands and gaze. Value = '领航组合驾驶辅助（NOA）功能需开展累计不少于72小时的有效道路试验' (>=72 h road tests). Data recording (DSSCDA) mandatory; accident-data part delayed 1 year.

items.customer_relevance: 5 Series rival moving to HEV + BEV versions; reliability/comfort focus.
items.quote: the fully redesigned new ES, which leads our next-generation electrified vehicle lineup
items.notes: Launch dates not given in source.

items.headline: Lexus LS retired after 2026 Heritage Edition
items.driver: Sales declined over time.
items.customer_relevance: Traditional Japanese luxury sedan demand vanished; flagship sedan segment thinning.
items.quote: just 691 units sold in the first half of 2025
items.notes: 250 Heritage Editions for US, from $99,280.

items.headline: Lexus US Q2 sales down 7.5%; June record
items.driver: Not stated; electrified +6.5%.
items.customer_relevance: Hybrid demand still rising in US premium.
items.quote: Second-quarter sales of 88,760 vehicles, down 7.5% on both a volume and DSR basis.
items.notes: Q2 electrified 37,300 (+6.5%). No H1 or model tables readable.

items.headline: Toyota+Lexus H1 down 2.9%, China -17%
items.driver: 17% plunge in China.
items.customer_relevance: Hybrid share >54% shows electrified (non-plug) demand.
items.quote: Global sales of Toyota- and Lexus-branded vehicles combined fell by 2.9% to 5,008,898 units year-to-date
items.notes: No Lexus-only H1 global figure found; combined brands, not comparable to Lexus FY item.

items.headline: Lexus ES outsold BMW 3 Series in US in 2025
items.driver: Not stated; all-new ES confirmed.
items.customer_relevance: US midsize luxury sedan buyers value reliability, comfort and hybrid economy.
items.quote: outsold the 3 by about 21%
items.notes: 3 Series 33,031 (single source). Published June 2026.

items.headline: Genesis US sales 82,331, fifth straight year of growth
items.driver: Not stated; product range and value.
items.customer_relevance: Value-luxury with long warranty attracts US buyers away from Germans.
items.quote: Genesis sold 82,331 vehicles in the US in 2025, its first time surpassing 80,000.
items.notes: yoy calculated from 75,003 (2024). Lincoln ~100,000 (expected), Acura ~130,000.

items.headline: Genesis adds hybrids and EREV after dropping electrified G80
items.driver: Electrified G80 dropped; slower BEV demand.
items.customer_relevance: US premium buyers pushed toward hybrids/EREV over converted BEVs.
items.quote: Genesis is launching its first hybrid, the GV80, this year, followed by the GV70 hybrid in early 2027.
items.notes: Also GV70-based EREV and GV90 flagship BEV expected.

items.headline: Electrified G80 pulled from US after under 400 sales
items.driver: Converted ICE platform; weak demand.
items.customer_relevance: Executive-sedan buyers reject converted BEVs; dedicated platforms matter.
items.quote: Genesis sold fewer than 400 copies in the U.S. last year.
items.notes: Value is an upper bound ('fewer than 400').

items.headline: JLR retail sales down 25% after cyber attack
items.driver: Production stoppages after cyber incident, US tariffs, legacy Jaguar wind-down.
items.customer_relevance: Luxury buyers concentrate on Range Rover/Defender; Jaguar absent.
items.quote: Retail sales for the third quarter of 79,600 units (including CJLR) were down 25.1% year-on year
items.notes: JLR Q3 FY26 = Oct-Dec 2025. Wholesale 59,200 (-43.3%).

items.headline: JLR North America retail down 38%
items.driver: Cyber incident and incremental US tariffs.
items.customer_relevance: Tariffs hurt UK-built luxury imports.
items.quote: incremental US tariffs impacting JLR's US exports, continued to impact volumes.
items.notes: Wholesale NA -64.4%. Region = North America.

items.headline: JLR China retail down 18%
items.driver: Cyber incident; market.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese luxury demand for imports weak.
items.quote: China -46.0% [wholesale] -18.4% [retail]
items.notes: Value read from the release's sales table; quote reproduces the table row.

items.headline: Range Rover/Sport/Defender 74.3% of JLR wholesales
items.driver: Focus on profitable luxury nameplates.
items.customer_relevance: Luxury buyers pay for strong iconic brands.
items.quote: The overall mix of Range Rover, Range Rover Sport and Defender models was 74.3% of total wholesale volumes in Q3 FY26.

items.headline: JLR Q4 FY26 retail down 14%; FY26 retail -17.8%
items.driver: Planned wind-down of legacy Jaguar models.
items.customer_relevance: Brand relaunch gap reduces choice for luxury buyers.
items.quote: Retail: 92,700 units (including CJLR), down 14.3% year-on-year
items.notes: Secondary source (T3) citing JLR. FY26 retail 352,300 (-17.8%); FY26 wholesale 307,900 (-23.2%). China retail -34.6% in Q4.

items.headline: JLR Q1 FY27 retail down 15%
items.driver: Supplier fire, Middle East conflict, Jaguar wind-down ahead of Type 01.
items.customer_relevance: Luxury demand shaken by geopolitics; supply resilience matters.
items.quote: Retail sales in Q1 FY27 were 80,000* units, down 15.3% vs Q1 FY26.
items.notes: Q1 FY27 = Apr-Jun 2026. Wholesale 79,300 (-9.2%).

items.headline: JLR North America retail down 13%
items.driver: Not stated per region.
items.customer_relevance: US luxury import demand recovering slightly vs Q3 FY26.
items.quote: North America (-13.1%)
items.notes: Retail by region list. Wholesale NA flat.

items.headline: JLR China retail down 24%
items.driver: Not stated per region.
items.customer_relevance: China luxury import decline deepening.
items.notes: Retail by region list.

items.headline: Range Rover/Sport/Defender reach 80.8% of wholesales
items.driver: Strong mix of core luxury nameplates.
items.customer_relevance: Luxury buyers concentrate on iconic SUVs.
items.quote: The strong mix of Range Rover, Range Rover Sport and Defender models continued in Q1 FY27

items.headline: Cadillac claims best-selling luxury EV brand; best retail since 2007
items.driver: Full EV SUV lineup (Optiq, Lyriq, Vistiq, Escalade IQ); EV demand pulled forward before credit expiry.
items.customer_relevance: US luxury EV buyers accept domestic EV SUVs; Tesla excluded from claim.
items.quote: GM claimed Cadillac was the best-selling luxury EV brand after sales rose 69% in 2025.
items.notes: Ambiguous whether +69% is EV or total; other secondary sources give ~49k EVs (+69%), ~28% share. Total 2025 sales conflict (147,214 vs 173,516) unresolved.

items.headline: Cadillac US Q2 sales down 19%
items.driver: Discontinued XT4 and XT6; tariff pull-ahead comparison.
items.customer_relevance: Removing affordable ICE crossovers costs volume; EV lineup alone can't fill gap.
items.quote: Overall, Cadillac sales were down 19.2% for the quarter and are off 22.3% year-to-date.
items.notes: Q2 2025 base 44,347. CT5 sedan outsold most crossovers.

items.headline: Cadillac best Q2 EV sales; Lyriq -18%, Optiq +43% H1
items.driver: Smaller/cheaper EVs (Optiq) grow; Lyriq declines.
items.customer_relevance: Lower-priced luxury EVs sell better after credit expiry.
items.quote: The Lyriq remains Cadillac's top-selling EV, with 7,578 units sold (-18%)

items.headline: 24 EVs lost 38% vs WLTP on average at −32 °C
items.driver: NAF El Prix winter test in Folldal, Norway.
items.customer_relevance: Real winter range is far below WLTP; Nordic/North China/US-north buyers need efficient heat pumps and honest range display.
items.quote: a 38% reduction
items.notes: Same test as Jan item; this aggregate figure was published after Jan cut-off.

items.headline: US EV share record 10.5% in Q3 2025 before credit expiry
items.driver: Pull-forward before federal EV tax credit expired 30 Sep 2025; 438,487 units.
items.customer_relevance: US BEV demand was incentive-driven; without credit, PHEV/ICE options matter more for US successors.
items.quote: electric cars accounted for 10.5 per cent of total car sales in the US

items.headline: US EV share falls to 5.8% in Q4 2025 after credit ends
items.driver: Post-credit plunge: 234,000 units, −46% QoQ, −36% YoY; FY2025 share 7.8%; Cox expected ~8% in 2026.
items.customer_relevance: US BEV appetite soft; successors need flexible powertrain offer in US.
items.quote: total EV sales in Q4 plunged to 234,000 units ... then fell to 5.8% in Q4
items.notes: yoy_pct refers to units. CarEdge reports 5.7%.

items.headline: US EV share stuck at ~5.8% in Q2 2026; hybrids forecast +9%
items.driver: 247,226 EVs (KBB est.), −20.5% YoY, +14.7% vs Q1; hybrid sales forecast to rise ~9%.
items.customer_relevance: Cox's ~8% 2026 outlook from January not met by mid-year; US buyers favour hybrids—PHEV/HEV variants matter for US derivatives.
items.quote: EV sales accounted for approximately 5.8% of total new-vehicle volume in the second quarter.
items.notes: yoy_pct refers to units. Hybrid +9% forecast phrased by fetch tool as 'first half of 2026'; search snippet said 'in 2026' - ambiguous.

items.headline: EU proposes 90% 2035 CO2 target; PHEVs, EREVs may stay
items.driver: Commission Automotive Package: remaining 10% offset via EU low-carbon steel, e-fuels, biofuels; new small-EV category up to 4.2 m.
items.customer_relevance: PHEV/EREV variants remain viable in Europe beyond 2035; customers keep powertrain choice.
items.quote: plug-in hybrids, range extenders, mild hybrids, and internal combustion engine vehicles can continue to be sold beyond 2035
items.notes: Proposal, not adopted law; status by 2026-07 not verified.

items.headline: China EREV sales fall three months running as BEVs improve
items.driver: New BEVs average >500 km range; 12.82m chargers end-2024; cheaper batteries. Li Auto down five months.
items.customer_relevance: In China, range anxiety fading as BEV range and charging improve; EREV appeal declining for premium.
items.quote: The average range of newly launched EVs in 2025 exceeds 500 km
items.notes: Value = Sep 2025 domestic EREV sales, yoy −13%. Share rose 3.6% (2021) to 9.1% (2024).

items.headline: China EREV sales topped 1.2m in 2025; stricter EREV standard coming
items.driver: New QC/T1086-2026 range-extender standard effective 1 Nov 2026 (durability, generator control).
items.customer_relevance: EREV still large in China; LWB/rear-comfort buyers may value long-range EREV, but momentum is slowing.
items.quote: surpassing 1.2 million units in 2025
items.notes: Value is 'over 1.2m' (lower bound). Secondary summaries cite CPCA May 2026 EREV wholesale 95,000 (−24.9% YoY) - not fetched.

items.headline: Huawei/JAC Maextro S800 sets Chinese rear-seat luxury benchmark
items.driver: Zero-gravity rear seats (20-way, 148.5° recline), massage, privacy screen partition, fridge; BEV and EREV.
items.customer_relevance: China LWB buyers benchmark rear lounge comfort against domestic rivals; relevant for G68/G70 successors.
items.quote: zero-gravity seats with 20-way electric adjustment, up to 148.5° recline
items.notes: Price range 708,000–1,018,000 CNY.

items.headline: Maextro S800 ~2,600 sales in Jan 2026, ~2x Maybach S / 7 Series
items.driver: Price and technology vs Maybach/Panamera; 14,000+ cumulative since mid-2025 debut.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese luxury buyers accept a domestic tech-led rear-seat flagship; 7 Series China positioning is under pressure.
items.quote: Tylko w styczniu 2026 roku Maextro S800 znalazł ponad 2600 nabywców ... Mercedes-Maybach klasy S i BMW serii 7 osiągnęły wyniki niemal o połowę niższe.
items.notes: Low-tier source, single month; 'BMW 7 Series ~half' is approximate per source. Cross-check with CPCA/insurance data.

items.headline: Willingness to pay for connected services drops to 68%
items.driver: S&P Global Mobility connected car survey: from 86% (2024) to 68% (2025); frustration with paywalled built-in hardware.
items.customer_relevance: Feature-on-demand for hardware already in the car risks backlash; bundle core comfort features into purchase price.
items.quote: from 86% in 2024 to 68% in 2025
items.notes: No 2026 edition found.

items.headline: CarPlay Ultra launches on Aston Martin; Mercedes won't use it
items.driver: Three years after announcement; Hyundai, Kia, Genesis signed up.
items.customer_relevance: Deep phone-OS takeover of all screens is available; BMW must decide how far to open its HMI to Apple.
items.quote: the Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis brands have signed up to make it compatible in their vehicles.

items.headline: CarPlay Ultra still Aston-only; Audi, Volvo, Polestar, Renault drop out
items.driver: Per FT; 13 brands incl. Porsche, Genesis, Hyundai, Ford list intent; BMW not on list.
items.customer_relevance: Most premium OEMs keep own HMI; strong standard CarPlay/Android Auto reliability matters more (see IQS 2026).
items.quote: Audi, Volvo, Polestar, and Renault have also decided against supporting CarPlay Ultra.
items.notes: BMW reportedly played down interest (secondary, not verified).
